Chapter 5
Integrating with Production Planning
When a customer registers a product complaint, it’s far easier for the
company to trace the origin of raw materials used in production when
QM is an integral part of the production process.
You have the option to integrate QM into several production processes as deemed
applicable to the business requirements. Companies implementing QM are uniquely
positioned to take advantage of various checks and balances on the quality of materials
being produced. This ensures that there are no raw materials released to production
until quality specifications have been adhered to and that no finished goods are dis-
patched to the customer until they meet the quality standards set by the company.
When defective goods are produced, quality issues not only affect the quality of the
final goods produced but also result in loss of machine and man hours. Companies
integrating QM in their production processes have access to a vast amount of data and
information to help them make long-term decisions.
This chapter begins by covering the configuration basics of setting up QM with produc-
tion planning (PP). Then, the focus shifts to required QM master data and culminates in
running the entire end-to-end business process of the production cycles. As you’ve
seen the master data creation processes extensively in Chapter 2, here we provide the
QM master data checklist only to ensure that it’s available in the system.
Table 5.1 describes the various inspection types used in production processes that can
also be used in QM. We’ll cover all these inspection types and their applications in this
chapter.
Inspection Type Inspection Plan Usage Inspection Type Description
02 6 Goods issue inspection
03 1 In-process inspection for process order
04 5 Final inspection for goods receipt from produc-
tion
13 1 In-process inspection for run schedule header
Table 5.1 Inspection Types in Production Planning

5 Integrating with Production Planning
282
Note
The focus and examples of QM integration with PP in this chapter are on production
planning for process industries (PP-PI). However, it’s important to note that the same
configuration, master data, business process concepts, and fundamentals apply
equally to the discrete manufacturing (shop floor control) production type. Where
there is any difference, it will be specifically highlighted.
5.1 Configuration Basics
The following sections discuss the configuration settings that you need to ensure are
available in the system to integrate QM with PP.
5.1.1 Material Type/Task List Combination
If the company uses the standard material types, such as raw materials (ROH), finished
goods (FERT), or trading goods (HAWA), then their task list types are available in the
system. However, if any material type that you want to go through the quality inspec-
tion and control process (e.g., spare parts [ERSA] or company-specific material types) is
not available, then you need to ensure that the combination of task list type Q and the
material type exists in the system. To do so, follow configuration menu path SAP IMG 
Quality Management  QM Planning  Inspection Planning  Assign Task List Type to
Material Type. Choose New Entries, add the material type/task list type combination,
and save your entries.
5.1.2 Order Type-Dependent Plant Parameters
Process order creation signals to the production department to start production of the
material and to check the material’s quantity during various stages of production. The
process order quantity denotes the target or planned quantity for production. When
the production department has actually produced some or all of the target/planned
quantity, it proceeds to confirm this produced quantity in the SAP S/4HANA system.
Although there are more PP-specific settings to enable the system to control different
functions during process order creation, you make a single setting that is specific to QM.
To set up order type-dependent plant parameters, use Transaction COR4 or follow menu
path SAP IMG  Production  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Order 
Master Data  Order  Define Order Type-Dependent Plant Parameters (see Figure 5.1).
Figure 5.1 shows the Planning tab for plant 1710 and order type YBM2. Incorporate
inspection type 03 to enable the system to perform in-process (during production)
inspection of the material.

Tips and Tricks
If you’ve configured any other inspection types of inspection origin 03, then these will
also appear in the dropdown list for you to choose from.
5.1.3 Confirmation Parameters
When you perform confirmation against a process order, whether it’s for an entire
order or milestone confirmation, the system makes actual data updates of the yield,
scrap, and rework objects.

5 Integrating with Production Planning
284
The confirmation process comprises the quantity produced at each phase of the pro-
duction process. If there are quality checks and steps involved in the production pro-
cess, then you can control whether the system adheres to the sequence of quality
inspections with the configuration settings of confirmation parameters.
Example
After you mix paint, you want the quality inspector to inspect the mixed paint and
record the results. Unless this step is ensured, the system shouldn’t allow the produc-
tion person to confirm the next step of production. Further, if you have another step in
which the quality inspector must check for filled-up paint cans before they are packed
and sealed, then you can control these sequences of steps via the confirmation param-
eters’ control.
To set up parameters for order confirmation, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production 
Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Order  Operations  Confirmation 
Define Confirmation Parameters.
Figure 5.2 shows the parameters for the order confirmation for plant 1710 and order
type YBM2. To ensure that the system adheres to confirming various phases of process
order and according to the defined sequence, set the operation sequence to E Error
when operation sequence is not adhered to. We’ll show how it works in Section 5.3.1.
Figure 5.2 QM-Specific Settings in Order Confirmation
© 

285
5.1 Configuration Basics
Similarly, set the Results Rec. (QM) to 1 Error message if no insp. results exist. This set-
ting ensures that unless the quality inspection record results in an in-process inspec-
tion, the system doesn’t allow confirmation of that specific phase. You’ll see how this
setting works in Section 5.3.2.
Note
During the SAP S/4HANA system implementation project, you discuss, evaluate, and
agree with the client on the level of controls required and then make the necessary set-
tings. In general, the control should neither be too loose nor too stringent to compro-
mise the day-to-day work of business process owners. The level of control also depends
on the stability of production and quality processes, as well as business maturity, for
optimal production without comprising on quality controls.
5.1.4 Control Key
With the relevant settings in the control key, you can control whether inspection char-
acteristics are required or optional and whether the system is to undertake automatic
goods receipt. Parameters also exist for scheduling, costing, and printing that are more
relevant to PP than QM. Finally, you can also control how the system processes the con-
firmations.
To set the required parameters of the control key, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality
Management  Quality Planning  Inspection Planning  Operation  Define Control Keys
for Inspection Operations (see Figure 5.3).
Figure 5.3 Control Key for Operations

5 Integrating with Production Planning
286
Table 5.2 lists the details about the functions that occur when you enable any field by
selecting the relevant checkbox.
In general, there is no need to specifically configure control keys in QM; rather, you
need to coordinate with a PP resource (or consultant) to enable you to integrate QM-
related processes in production. We’ll show you how configuration settings made for
control key QM04 apply in the business process for in-process quality inspection
(inspection type 03). In Section 5.2.2, you’ll see the actual use of a control key in a mas-
ter recipe, and then in business processes.
Field Details
Scheduling Enables scheduling of operations in a routing or master recipe.
Print confirmation Enables the option to print a process order confirmation (the quantity
produced in a shift).
Det. Cap. Reqmnts Enables capacity requirements planning in the production process.
Print Enables printing of shop floor papers.
Insp. Char. Required Requires that a master inspection characteristic be assigned to a rout-
ing or master recipe. Master inspection characteristics entered for a
phase or operation then become the basis of results recording for in-
process inspection.
Cost Enables cost calculation for an activity.
Automatic GR Enables automatic goods receipt when you confirm a process order.
Sched. External Op. Enables the provision to enter scheduling data for external operations
such as subcontracting or third-party processing.
Print Time Tickets Enables printing of operation- and phase-level details of shop floor
papers.
Rework Enables the option to “rework” a process order.
External Processing Option to allow or disallow external processing of operations for a
process order.
Confirmations Dropdown option to allow or disallow confirmation of operations. If
you want the system to adhere to an operation’s sequence during con-
firmation, then you need to choose 2 Confirmation required. If you’re
using PP-PI, then the same principle applies to the phases’ confirma-
tion (instead of the operations’ confirmation, which applies to shop
floor control).

5.2 Master Data
Tips and Tricks
To ensure that you can incorporate master inspection characteristics for in-process
inspection (during production), select the Insp. Char. Required checkbox.
5.2 Master Data
Although significant master data pertaining to PP is managed by the PP team, the
focus of this section is to show where, specifically, QM integrates with PP. During the
SAP S/4HANA implementation project, QM consultants (or business users) coordinate
with the PP team to incorporate the required QM master data (e.g., inspection charac-
teristics) into the PP master data (e.g., master recipe or routing).
5.2.1 Production Planning and Quality Management Master Data Checklist
The following is the PP master data that you need to ensure is available in the system:
 Material master
 Bill of materials (BOM)
 Master recipe, rate routing, or routing
 Production version
The QM master data that you need in the system is as follows:
 Inspection types 03 and 04 active in the QM view of the material master of the fin-
ished good
 Inspection type 02 active in the QM view of the material master of the raw material
or semifinished good
 Inspection plan usage 5 (for inspection type 04) and 6 (for inspection type 02), both
with status 4 (for released)
 No inspection plan needed for inspection type 03
5.2.2 QM Data in Master Recipe
A master recipe uses something called a phase, which works in the same manner as
operations do in routing for discrete manufacturing. It’s easier to maintain detailed
levels working at the phase level in the master recipe because you can manage and
incorporate more production and quality details.
In the master recipe, you assign activities such as production duration or labor hours at
the phase level and not at the operation level. Therefore, the confirmation of a process
order is recorded for a phase and not an operation. You also assign a resource (work

5 Integrating with Production Planning
288
center) at the operation level. The phases below the operation then adopt the resource
that you assign at the operation level. The system assigns the standard values and
activities (controlled by a control key in the resource) as active at the phase level and
not at the operation level. You can, however, integrate in-process quality inspections of
QM at either the operation level or the phase level.
Tips and Tricks
For process manufacturing, we suggest that you integrate QM with PP at the phase
level because it offers better controls and visibility, which we’ll show in this chapter.
For discrete manufacturing, QM integration with PP for in-process inspection takes
place at an operation level.
To create a master recipe for which the production version already exists, use Transac-
tion C201 or follow menu path Logistics  Production—Process  Master Data  Master
Recipes  Recipe and Material List  Create. On the initial screen of the master recipe,
enter Material “SG2200”, Plant “1710”, and Production Version “0001”, and the header
screen appears.
Figure 5.4 shows the Operations tab of the master recipe, in which the operation is
0010. Enter the Resource “QCLAB” at the operation level, and the system automatically
copies it into all the phases below it. The system denotes phase 0040 by the Phase
checkbox. When you define an operation as a phase, you also have to define the supe-
rior operation, which, for this example, is 0030 (the operation). Operation 0010 and
phase 0020 refer to the production process of filling (not shown), but it’s operation
0030 and phase 0040 (the superior operation of which is 0030) that are relevant to
QM.
Notice the control key QM04, the settings of which you previously made in Section
5.1.4. The system should adhere to the sequence of operations (essentially the same as
phases in PP-PI) during confirmation; therefore, you must first confirm phase 0020,
then phase 0040, and so on. If you deviate from or miss the phases’ confirmation
sequence, the system displays an error message and doesn’t allow you to proceed fur-
ther. Similarly, if you don’t record the results of phases 0020 and 0040, the system
doesn’t allow you to confirm the respective phases.
Because this is an in-process inspection, you also need to enter the master inspection
characteristics that then form the basis of your results recording and usage decision. To
enter master inspection characteristics, choose a relevant phase, such as 0040, and
choose Inspection Characteristic, and the system brings up the screen shown in Figure
5.5. Here, you can enter the QM data elements, such as master inspection characteris-
tics, maintain their values as shown in Figure 5.4, and save your settings.

Figure 5.4 Master Recipe
Figure 5.5 Quality Data in Master Recipe
Tips and Tricks
For the system to ensure it adheres to the defined phases during the confirmation pro-
cess, you must maintain a predecessor-successor relationship between any two
phases. To maintain the relationship of one phase to another, select the desired phase
(e.g., phase 0040), and choose the Relationship icon (the chain link icon) shown in
Figure 5.4. Once on the detailed screen of a phase relationship of phase 0040, enter the
predecessor phase, which in this example is “0020”; here the relationship type needs
to be “FS” (finish-start), which means that phase 0020 needs to finish before phase
0040 can start.
For shop floor control (discrete manufacturing), there’s no such requirements for main-
taining relationships among operations in a routing.

5 Integrating with Production Planning
290
Tips and Tricks
If the production process also entails external processing, such as subcontracting, and
if you must also perform quality inspection for it, then in the phase details that involve
subcontracting, you can assign inspection type 0060 to enable you to integrate QM in
the subcontracting process (external processing). For example, to enter external pro-
cessing details in the screen in Figure 5.4, choose Phase 0060 and then choose Operat.
Details (the magnifying glass icon). In the General Data tab, enter the external process-
ing (subcontracting) details and inspection type 0130.
Refer to Chapter 4, Section 4.5, in which we cover the end-to-end business process of
subcontracting (external processing) and how to put inspection type 0130 to use.
Note
For discrete manufacturing (shop floor control), use Transaction CA01 to create a routing.
For QM integration with PP in discrete manufacturing, you assign the master inspection
characteristics at the operation level. To create a rate routing of a material in repetitive
manufacturing (REM), use Transaction CA21; the process of assigning master inspection
characteristics at the operation level is the same as in discrete manufacturing.
5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning
In the following sections, we’ll cover the end-to-end business processes in PP, beginning
with process order creation, quality inspection upon goods issue, and the in-process
inspection, followed by quality inspection upon goods receipt into the warehouse.
5.3.1 Process Manufacturing and Discrete Manufacturing
Figure 5.6 shows an end-to-end business process for production execution in which
QM integrates into the following all important steps:
1 A process order (or production order in shop floor control) is created.
2 Goods are issued out to begin the production process.
3 However, before the production operator uses the issued-out material, a quality
check is put in place. This is via inspection lot creation upon goods issue, and the
inspection type is 02, which must be quality cleared.
4 The actual production begins, and further quality checks must ensue for in-process
inspection or during production inspection. This is ensured via inspection lot cre-
ation wth inspection type 03.
5 The goods are produced and delivered or received at the warehouse.
6 At this stage, another round of quality checks takes place to ensure that the deliv-
ered finished goods meet quality standards. For this, the system creates an inspec-
tion lot with inspection type 04.
© 

291

material document number 4900007692 and process order number 1002145. This
inspection type isn’t stock-based, so the quality inspection steps are results recording
and usage decision.
Warning
If the material is rejected during goods issue inspection (inspection type 02), there is no
way for the system to control that it’s not to be used further in the production process.
To ensure better controls, you must return the issued-out defective material back to
the warehouse using the Return Delivery option. For return delivery, use Transaction
MIGO (refer to Figure 5.11 again), and select Return Delivery and then Material Docu-
ment from the dropdown lists at the top. Enter the material document number, which
in this example is “4900007692” (the same document number against which you
issued the material from the warehouse). The relevant movement type for return deliv-
ery is 262. In the return delivery option, you can also control the quantity of defective
material that you’re returning to the warehouse.

5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning
Confirmation
To bring greater visibility to the production process and the quality steps involved, you
periodically confirm the produced quantity at a resource or work center. The frequen-
cies with which you confirm an operation, phase, or order depend entirely on business
needs. For example, in 24 hours, you can confirm the quantities produced at the end of
an eight-hour shift. This means you have to perform two partial confirmations and
then one final confirmation. When you perform the final confirmation, the system no
longer expects any further confirmations against the operation or the order.
To proceed with confirmation of a time ticket, use Transaction COR6N or follow menu
path Logistics  Production—Process  Process Order  Confirmation  Enter for Phase 
Time Ticket.
Note
For time ticket confirmation in discrete manufacturing (shop floor control), use Trans-
action CO11N.
Figure 5.13 shows the initial screen to confirm the time ticket. Enter the Order number
as “1002145”, enter the Phase as “0060”, and press (Enter).
Figure 5.13 Time Ticket Confirmation of a Process Order

5 Integrating with Production Planning

We deliberately enter the Phase as “0060” to check whether the configuration you
undertook for operation/phase sequence adherence in Figure 5.2 is working. The sys-
tem displays an error message, as shown at the bottom of the screen. This means you
have to first confirm the phase as 0020, which is the first phase in Figure 5.4. So, you
undertake the phase-wise confirmation as shown in Figure 5.4 while also ensuring that
before you confirm phase 0060, you’ve recorded results for that operation/phase.
Figure 5.14 shows the error message that appears when you try to confirm a phase with-
out first recording results of phase 0040. Again, this is due to the settings that you
made in Figure 5.3, which stipulates that unless the QM results are first entered for the
phase, the system doesn’t allow you to confirm the phase. All these quality controls,
checks, and balances during the production process help you manage quality aspects of
production, thereby minimizing or eliminating in-process or produced goods rejec-
tions.
Figure 5.14 Error Message Indicating QM Data Is Missing
In-Process Inspection: Inspection Type 03
Figure 5.15 shows the in-process inspection lot number 30000000555 for process
order number 1002145. As already mentioned, the in-process inspection for production

same that you saw in Figure 5.8, such as inspection lot number and batch number.
Inspection lots of inspection type 03 aren’t stock-relevant, so you need to record

Note
You can also integrate QM business processes of in-process inspections using process

material SG2200.

For a flexible in-process inspection, you can have the system create inspection lot char-
acteristics for released production order operations. Therefore, changes to unreleased
order operations are still possible and are reflected in the inspection lot as soon as they
are released. This allows for a flexible in-process or in-production inspection. To use
this feature, follow the menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Basic Settings 
Maintain Settings at Client Level. In the Further Settings area of the screen, select the
Late Characteristic Creation checkbox.
Goods Receipt for Process Order
Once the goods are produced for a process order, you deliver them to the warehouse so
that the warehouse staff can record the goods receipt. On goods receipt, the system cre-
ates an inspection lot of inspection type 04 with reference to the process order 1002145.
Access the screen in Figure 5.16 via Transaction MIGO, and select Goods Receipt and
then Order from the dropdown lists at the top. Then, enter process order number
“1002145” in the blank box. The movement type for goods receipt against a process
order is 101 and is shown at the top-right corner of the screen. Save your entries, and
the system creates material document number 5000000018.
Figure 5.16 Goods Receipt for Process Order

The inspection lot consists of relevant details, such as material document number
5000002463 and process order number 1002145. This inspection type is stock-relevant,
so the quality steps are results recording (and any defects recording), usage decision,

Tips and Tricks
You can also let the system create an early inspection lot for inspection type 04 at the
time of creating, or release a process or production order so that you can inspect the
goods and record its results before posting them in stock. To do so, choose Early Inspec-
tion Lot Creation for Order Item in the Control InsLot (inspection lot) field from the
dropdown list while activating inspection type 04 in material master. This entire pro-
cess is known as early inspection lot creation for a process or production order.
5.3.2 Repetitive Manufacturing
Repetitive manufacturing (REM) finds greater application in production scenarios with
high repetition rates, high product stability, and low product complexity. REM is char-
acterized by quantity-based and period-based production (uninterrupted production
over a longer period of time). In this section, we’ll cover the important REM processes
of not just PP but also QM. Either the system automatically creates inspection lots or
you have to undertake the relevant business process steps.
Figure 5.18 shows the end-to-end REM business processes:
1 Create the REM planned order (also interchangeably referred to as the run schedule
header).
2 Create the QM inspection lot of inspection type 13 for the in-process inspection.
3 The confirmation process ensures goods issue and goods receipt (depending on the
settings made in the REM profile).
4 On goods receipt, the system creates another inspection lot of inspection type 04.

5.3 Business Processes in Production Planning
PP and QM Master Data Checklist
The following is the PP master data that you need to ensure is available in the system:
 Material master
 BOM
 Rate routing or routing
 Production version
The QM master data that you need in the system is as follows:
 Inspection types 13 and 04 active in the QM view of the material master
 Inspection plan usage 5 (for inspection type 04) with status 4 (for released)
Note
For in-process inspection of inspection type 13, there is no need to create an inspection
plan (Transaction QP01) for the material. This is because you already incorporate the
relevant master inspection characteristics in the operations of routing or rate routing
of the material.
Run Schedule Header
The production team often has to make changes to the existing planning elements,
such as planned orders, or create new planned orders to account for production con-
straints or other practical realities, such as an unplanned plant or machine shutdown.
This example uses an already created REM planned order 2694 and continues with the
remaining business processes, with greater focus on QM integration in the REM pro-
duction type.
Tips and Tricks
You can use Transaction MD11 to create a REM-planned order. On the initial screen for
Planned Order Profile, choose LA-Stock Order. Enter Material “FG233”, Plant “1710”, and
Order Quantity “100” kg, and save.
In-Process Inspection for Run Schedule Header: Inspection Type 13
With the planned order for the material already available in the system, you can now
proceed to create an in-process inspection lot for the REM-planned order (run schedule
header). It’s important to note that for in-process inspection in REM, the system doesn’t
consider the quantity of the REM-planned order that you previously created. Rather, the
system creates an inspection quantity based on a material/plant/production version

5 Integrating with Production Planning
302
combination. So, the quantity details that you enter for the production version become
the basis for the system to calculate inspection lot quantity.
To create an inspection lot for in-process inspection for the REM-planned order, use
Transaction MFPR or follow menu path Quality Management  Quality Inspection 
Worklist  Inspection Lot Creation  Inspection Lots for Prod. Versions (see Figure 5.19).
Here you see the initial screen for inspection lot processing of materials produced
using the REM production type. Choose the QM Active radio button so that the system
brings up the materials with QM active, and enter Plant “1710”, Material Number
“FG233”, and Production Version “0001”. Choose Execute, which leads to Figure 5.20.
Figure 5.20 shows that the last inspection lot the system created for material FG233 and
plant 1710 was 130000000000. The red signal light indicates that the results recording
and usage decision for inspection lot 130000000000 are already made, and the sys-
tem is now ready to create a new inspection lot. The fact that a usage decision for

Repetitive Manufacturing Assembly Confirmation
A REM confirmation indicates that you’ve performed actual production and are now
entering the details of the goods produced in the system. It’s important to note that
during the assembly backflush, the system automatically posts the component con-
sumptions (goods issue).
Depending on how the PP team has set up the REM profile and assigned it to the mate-
rial, the system performs the necessary functions. It also often makes sense to use
reporting point confirmation to post the withdrawal of components and production
activities at an earlier stage and after operations are already completed.
When you post the goods receipt for the finished parts during confirmation, the sys-
tem performs several different actions by default (these are controlled to a large extent
using the REM profile).
To access the REM confirmation for an assembly backflush, use Transaction MFBF or
follow menu path Logistics  Production  Repetitive Manufacturing  Data Entry  Repet-
itive Manufacturing Confirmation (see Figure 5.23). On the initial screen of REM confir-
mation, select the Assembly backflush radio button. You use the screen to confirm the
production yield, as well as record component consumption and activities. In the
screen shown in Figure 5.23, you now perform the actual assembly backflush posting
for Material FG233, Plant 1710, and Production Version 0001. The yield confirmation for
the material in this REM assembly backflush is 10 kg.
Reporting point backflush in REM occurs when the system is able to automatically
backflush several operations in the processing sequence. Using the reporting point
backflush procedure, you can backflush components synchronized with actual con-
sumption as much as possible.

Note
If you have a specific business need to conduct a quality check on goods issue of the

the settings of the REM profile so that the goods issue and goods receipt steps aren’t
performed in the same step. It makes more sense to first issue out (goods issue) the
component for a reporting point, perform its quality inspection, and then, as a next
step, perform goods receipt subsequently (or at the end of production process) and on
another reporting point.
